title: Bidirectional LSTM Toxicity Classifier with Ranking Residuals
summary: The solution tokenizes lowercased comments into up to 256 word/punctuation tokens, builds a frequency-pruned training-only vocabulary, maps rare/unseen tokens to an unknown ID, and batches padded sequences by length. A learned embedding with word-vector dropout feeds two bidirectional LSTM layers. Masked max and mean pooling are concatenated, transformed by residual dense layers, and used for a toxicity logit and identity-label auxiliary logits. Training uses Adam, mixed precision, gradient clipping, decayed learning rate with a floor, weighted BCE on soft toxicity targets, and auxiliary identity BCE. Late model iterates are averaged and validation probabilities are produced with a sigmoid. A second configured stage freezes the selected encoder and initializes global and identity-bin-specific linear residual ranking heads. It samples subgroup/background positive-negative cells and optimizes pairwise ordering losses, optionally blended with a soft up/down/tie loss derived from fractional labels; bias-family cell losses emphasize weaker cells.
